text:
Connor Murphy came to Edmonton with a reputation built over 547 games in Chicago: a big right-shot defenseman who takes chances away. Under Mike Babcock he's playing almost 21 minutes a night and blocking a lot of shots, 58 in 26 games, the kind of volume that fits the label.

The five-on-five results don't fit it. The Oilers get 37% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with Murphy on the ice, almost 14 points worse than without him, and they've actually scored 4.0 more goals than those chances deserve during his shifts. If anything, the scoreboard has been kind. He has two assists and no goals, which was never going to be the measure of him.

The case for him lives in last season's numbers. Evolving-Hockey had him 56th among 215 defensemen, with opponents getting 0.19 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there (94th percentile), and noted he played with weaker teammates (bottom 8%), which drags raw on-ice numbers down. At 33, the question for the rest of the season is whether that version is still in there, or whether the blocks are now doing more of the work than the positioning.
